Tuesday, January 18, 2022  7:00 PM  Teleconference

NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that a Special Meeting of the Park & Activities Commission of the City of
Rolling Hills Estates will be held on Tuesday, January 18, 2021 at 7:00 p.m. via Video Teleconference. The
agenda for the special meeting with the items to be discussed is set forth below.

  Posted by the office of Community Services on Friday, January 14, 2021

Public Participation Information
  In accordance with Assembly Bill 361 (AB 361) and City Council Resolution No. 2487, due to the
  continuing state of emergency, including masking and social distancing directives as a result of the threat
  of the COVID-19 virus, this meeting is being held remotely via teleconference. There will not be a physical
  location for this meeting. Members of the public may participate in the meeting in the following ways:

  - Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1 669 900 6833) from any phone,
  Meeting ID: 895 9594 5089 Meeting Password: 355733. (Please note you will not have the ability to
  speak using the call in option from a phone line.)

  - Members of the public may also comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes &
  Videos” page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there
  will be an “eComment” button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to
  the City’s SpeakUp page. After you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda.
  These comments can be seen by the public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the
  record.

  - Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
  Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store),
  by entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 895 9594 5089, Meeting Password: 355733. Members
  of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the following
  process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at the
  lower portion of your screen. The City Clerk will send you a chat message to identify which item on the
  agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city.

MINUTES
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION SPECIAL MEETING
  JANUARY 18, 2022

  1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

  An adjourned meeting of the Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills
  Estates was called to order at 7:01 p.m. via teleconference, pursuant to the Governor’s
  Executive Order N-29-20.

  2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

  3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Bain, Ciarolla, McCormick, Persichina, Pope,
  Retz, Romanelli

  Commissioners Absent:  None

  City Staff Present:  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Maintenance Superintendent Mike Goldsmith
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas
  Community Services Coordinator Daniel A-Haja

  4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION REGULAR MEETING DRAFT
  MINUTES OF NOVEMBER 15, 2021

  Assistant City Manager (ACM) Davis noted the incorrect minutes were posted
  on the agenda and that the December 13, 2021 minutes will be brought to the
  February Commission meeting.

  5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

  None

  6.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  NEW PROGRAM PROPOSAL-LA KINGS

  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas provided a review of the staff report.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN asked for information as to the reason or need for the City
  to endorse these lessons. Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas responded
  that recreation departments partner with local businesses to bring awareness to
  recreation programs and provide classes that cannot typically be offered by a City.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA asked if this was similar to the High School
  Recreation program which runs through the City. ACM Davis noted it is like the
  Summer Swim Program the City promotes which is run with the YMCA and the
  School District.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked about the 80/20 split, how it works and the
  benefit to the City from the arrangement; and asked if the facility fee, instructor, and
  City fee include this split. Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas responded that
  80% of revenue will go to the instructor and 20% will go to the City for marketing
  the program and registration. She added that the instructor will receive $64.80 and
  the City will receive $16.20 per resident and $25.20 per non-resident. It allows the
PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  1
JANUARY 18, 2022
   City to take in revenue for administrative costs while offering classes to the public
  that would not normally be able to be run by the City. COMMISSIONER
  ROMANELLI asked who pays the facility for rink usage. Community Services
  Supervisor Pinuelas responded that it is a contractor owned facility, so the
  contractor is responsible for that cost.

  CHAIR POPE noted that the rink belongs to the contractor which is LA Kings and
  wanted to know if there were any other fees and if they would be waived. She also
  asked if a Memorandum of Understanding is required.

  ACM Davis responded that the City’s contractor agreement would be used and that
  this is common amongst many other cities, although new to the City. The main
  difference would be the facility rental fee would not be included as it is not the City’s
  facility and that the new fee structure would be taken to Council if approved.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ noted the pitching coaches for the Little League who train
  players in the Summer and do not have the 80/20 split and asked why the City
  needed to be involved in the class registrations as they are not involved with the
  Little League in the same manner. Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas noted
  the difference that the new class would not be held on City property and that
  partnering with businesses to offer classes that the City cannot provide themselves
  is common in other cities. She added that the City is currently taking registrations
  for its other contract classes such as dog obedience and tennis lessons. ACM
  Davis noted the City is not in the practice of allowing private entities to run
  programming at the park unless the usage of the pitching coaches is part of the
  Little League agreement and does not rely on the City for promotion.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA noted monitoring of unauthorized pitching lessons
  was attempted at Ernie Howlett Park in previous years but is difficult to monitor.
  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK asked about the City’s involvement in registration
  and marketing of the program. Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas
  responded that the City may do more outreach for the new program at the start and
  that City staff would handle the registrations. He asked about the liability of the
  program to which Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas responded the program
  would use the City’s registration form which includes the liability waiver and will hold
  the City as additionally insured. COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK added that he
  thinks this is a great program for the City.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN asked if the program had performance requirements and
  a minimum number of students, Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas
  responded that the minimum and maximum is set by the contractor and that
  evaluation of the program would be best done after a few sessions to help build
  proper numbers due to varying sports seasons throughout the year.

  Gabriella Weissmann-Fritts of the LA Kings noted the program is currently in place
  in the City of El Segundo at the Toyota Sports complex and that they have operated
  in Hermosa Beach, Hawthorne, and El Segundo recreation programs. The class is
  an introductory ice skating and hockey class which runs for four weeks and shows
  students how to get comfortable on the ice. As the student progresses, they can
  choose to move onto a private program for more lessons.

  CHAIR POPE noted the positive aspect of community outreach to spread word of
  the class.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK asked if the other cities are also receiving the
  80/20 split. Gabriella Weissmann-Fritts noted the program is similar in most cities
  with LA Kings making at least $63 and $65 per skater and the City charging their
  fees on top of that amount.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  2
JANUARY 18, 2022
   COMMISSIONER BAIN asked if other cities in the peninsula were also offered this
  rink. Gabriella Weissmann-Fritts responded that Rolling Hills Estates is the first
  City that was contacted but other Cities may be reached out to in the future.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked about the impact this program would have
  on the existing staff workload. Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas stated
  staff has begun evaluating how to manage programming and that tennis staff could
  also be involved in the intake of registrations which is currently done with other
  contract classes such as tennis. The program will take a few sessions to build.
  Staff will have time to gauge workload as program builds and may bring registration
  system options to a future meeting that could assist with potential workload. No
  additional staff will be needed to intake registrations at this time. ACM Davis noted
  the registration process can be improved and that current registrations would not
  be impacted by the additional program.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA asked what age groups the program would be
  geared to. Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas responded that the classes
  are for tots, youth, and adults.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN asked if the towns already working with LA Kings promote
  their classes. Gabriella Weissmann-Fritts responded that the classes are being re-
  contracted with other cities and may be the reason they are not currently on other
  cities’ websites. Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas added that most
  recreation departments advertise classes through printed recreation guides mailed
  to homes or available online and some offer information online through recreation
  registration systems.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
  MCCORMICK to:

  ACCEPT STAFF RECOMMENDATION TO APPROVE THE ADDITION OF
  THE LA KINGS ICE LEARN TO SKATE AND HOCKEY PROGRAMS AT
  THE PROMENADE ON THE PENINSULA MALL ICE SKATING RINK TO
  THE CITY’S RECREATION CLASS OFFERINGS AND TO RECOMMEND
  TO THE CITY COUNCIL TO AMEND THE CITY’S FEE AND CHARGES
  SCHEDULE TO ADD AN 80/20 CONTRACT SPLIT FEE FOR CONTRACT
  CLASSES.

  AYES: Bain, Ciarolla, McCormick, Persichina, Pope, Retz, Romanelli

  The motion carries.

  B.  PICKLEBALL COURT CONSIDERATIONS

  Community Services Coordinator A-Haja provided a brief overview of the staff
  report.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN is in favor of pickleball as she had played in a private club
  where demand was very high. She added that there is no way to make a pickleball
  reservation on the City website. She supports permanent use of two tennis courts
  for eight pickleball court lines and adding instructors like the current tennis program.
  She added that a simple reservation system would also help welcome more players.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI noted that two pickleball courts per tennis court
  were proposed whereas COMMISSIONER BAIN suggested four per tennis court.
  Community Services Coordinator A-Haja explained that the fencing around the
  tennis court may prohibit the amount of pickleball lines, but he would confirm with
  the resurfacing company. COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI wanted to clarify that
  adding the pickleball lines would not prevent people from playing tennis as we

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  3
JANUARY 18, 2022
   would need those courts for tennis tournaments. Community Services Coordinator
  A-Haja responded that that is correct, though the survey was not in favor of the
  sharing of the courts, the resurfacing company has suggested using a lighter color
  for the pickleball lines if sharing the courts. This would invite possible future league
  play with pickleball. ACM Davis added that a review of community services
  programs and the usage of courts. Staff could develop hours for pickleball use
  when court usage for tennis is further analyzed. COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI
  noted the peaks and valleys of court usage with league play and the peak hours of
  usage from 9 am to 12 pm and wants to be respectful of the current tennis leagues
  and players at the tennis club. He is in favor of the idea and a usage study and
  noted the growing popularity of the sport but wants to ensure we do not squeeze
  any tennis players out.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN is in favor of a study and suggested marketing the
  availability of permanent lines of those courts. She added the demand for pickleball
  is increasing as demand for tennis goes down and a growth in pickleball may occur
  as the community ages. She added that she doesn’t want to see tennis diminished
  but wants to make sure we study the data to make an informed decision.
  Adjustments to fit four courts per tennis court seems to be the standard at other
  clubs and should be looked in to further.

  CHAIR POPE noted the data may not be accurate based on temporary pickleball
  lines as COMMISSIONER BAIN pointed out players do not like the temporary lines.
  CHAIR POPE noted that data should be tracked once the permanent lines are in
  place in order to gain an accurate view of pickleball at the club.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK noted the popularity of pickleball at Jack Kramer
  Club and asked how much the basketball court and volleyball court are utilized and
  if those could be potential pickleball sites.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA noted the land near the basketball and volleyball
  courts is not stable enough to support courts. Coordinator A-Haja confirmed that
  information. COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI noted the ground swell concerns that
  currently occur at the tennis courts.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ noted the rise in pickleball play and is in favor of them at
  the club. He added that once people learn of the courts, he is positive they will be
  used.

  Audience Member Judy Bayer noted her group of tennis players are turning to
  pickleball as they age and that temporary lines were hard to set up and inaccurate.
  She added that no chalk was used, and players would trip on the tape used for
  lines. She said the survey was not known to a lot of the players she knew. Ms.
  Bayer shared that dedicated pickleball courts are much nicer that temporary lines
  or over tennis court lines and that Ernie Howlett would benefit from permanent lines.
  She added that court reservations are easily done on the phone and the color of
  the pickleball lines may need to be reconsidered and suggests looking at what
  South Bay Tennis Club uses. Other cities’ courts are in poor condition so Ernie
  Howlett’s maintained courts would attract more pickleball players. Groups are
  growing for the sport and morning and afternoon play is popular among her group.

  ACM Davis noted staff is asking for approval of permanent pickleball lines and that
  Staff would come back with a proposed pickleball program in the future.

  CHAIR POPE wanted to clarify the amount of the lines and nets as they go forward
  with the tennis court resurfacing.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN wanted to address the possibility of researching the
  addition of four pickleball courts per tennis court.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  4
JANUARY 18, 2022
   COMMISSIONER RETZ asked for clarification regarding the bids and if the lower
  bid did not include the pickleball striping. Community Services Coordinator A-Haja
  noted that both include pickleball striping. COMMISSIONER RETZ was in favor of
  permanent pickleball lines and to investigate what would be involved in moving the
  fencing to accommodate more pickleball lines.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked to identify which fencing was being
  referenced. Community Services Coordinator A-Haja responded that the perimeter
  fencing was in question and would need to be reassessed to fit four pickleball courts
  on one tennis court. COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI wants to start with two
  pickleball courts per tennis court so as not to distract from the tennis court lines.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN noted the standard is four courts per tennis court. If the
  increased demand is there, then using the maximum amount of space would aid
  the recreation program.

  COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA wants to decide how many courts we should have
  before we paint the lines.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK asked why courts 5 and 6 were preferred.
  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI responded those courts are also the least used and
  Community Services Coordinator A-Haja added those were the courts suggested
  by Tennis Pro Coach Bob. He added that the location would also not interfere with
  tennis league play. ACM Davis noted staff could meet with resurfacing vendor and
  Maintenance Superintendent in the following weeks to assess the space available
  and noted that four pickleball courts per tennis court is what has been commonplace
  in local clubs.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK suggested reaching out to other clubs to ask
  about complaints from their tennis players to assess the desire of pickleball lines
  overlayed on tennis courts.

  ACM Davis noted that if the recommendation is for staff to review and come back
  then no motion is required.

  CHAIR POPE agreed to that recommendation and thanked Judy Bayer for
  attending.

  C.  TENNIS COURT RESURFACING

  ACM Davis suggested bringing the report back upon pickleball court
  considerations. The Commission agreed and Chair so directed.

  D.  2022 CITY COUNCIL MEETING ATTENDANCE SCHEDULE

  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas gave a brief overview of the staff report.

  CHAIR POPE suggested assigning the positions and going in order of a rotation as
  done in previous years.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI agreed.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN asked what the purpose of attendance to City Council
  meetings was as no questions have been raised about Parks and Activities.

  COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA noted she was asked about horse riding ring rules
  and was asked to clarify rules by the Council when she attended in the past.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  5
JANUARY 18, 2022
   COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI agrees that not many questions are directed
  toward the Commission and was unsure if Planning Commission members
  attended.

  CHAIR POPE noted attending meetings allows the City Council to recognize the
  Commission and can help promote upcoming City events.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK noted an absence of the Planning Commission as
  well.

  ACM Davis explained that attendance was started years ago and has continued
  due to the Commission’s connection to numerous City events and the Equestrian
  Committee.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN would like to have Commissioners notified of meetings
  where they are needed and if staff could notify the appropriate Committee member
  of the agenda where their participation would be beneficial to the meeting.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK has not seen the Council ask Commissioners for
  questions.

  ACM Davis noted in person meetings may be better to encourage City Council
  questions but will consult the City Manager; staff will still assign Commissioners
  and notify them of agendas in advance.

  Community Services Coordinator A-Haja notified the Commissioners they would be
  emailed the assignments.

  COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA noted not being able to attend in March.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ suggested including the City Council agenda to the
  Commissioner assigned to that meeting to also serve as a reminder to attend.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI noted the weekly agenda identifies the
  Commissioner that attends the Council meeting and was emailed the agenda in the
  past. Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas has noted that staff can continue
  that practice.

  E.  COMMITTEE AND SUBCOMMITTEE ASSIGNMENTS

  Community Services Coordinator A-Haja provided an overview of the assignments.
  The Commission reviewed and determined the 2022 assignments as follows:

  2022 Standing Committee Representatives

  Equestrian Committee (Monthly as needed) ………...Ciarolla

  Traffic and Safety Committee (Quarterly as needed) …………. Romanelli

  Environmental Advisory Committee (Quarterly as needed) …… …………. Bain

  2022 Commission Subcommittee Members

  Tracy Austin Doubles Tennis Tournament Subcommittee…McCormick, Pope,
  Romanelli

  The Hills Are Alive Race Subcommittee………... Ciarolla, Persichina, Romanelli

  City Celebration Subcommittee…………………………. Retz, Ciarolla, Bain

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  6
JANUARY 18, 2022
   Peninsula Holiday Parade of Lights Subcommittee… Persichina, Pope, McCormick

  Youth Sports Subcommittee…………...…… Persichina, Pope, Romanelli

  2022 Adopt-A-Park Assignments

  Ernie Howlett Park……………………………Persichina

  Highridge Park………………………………………...Bain

  Rockbluff Park……………………………………...Romanelli

  Chandler & Pepperwood Parks……………………………………. Ciarolla

  Silver Spur Park………………………………………………………Pope

  Dapplegray & Chandler Preserve …………………………………...Retz

  George F Canyon Nature Center, Preserve & Taber Grove Preserve…. McCormick

  F.  PROPOSED 2022 SPECIAL EVENTS CALENDAR

  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas provided a brief overview of the special
  event calendar.

  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas noted the addition of community service
  components to some events as suggested by COMMISIONER MCCORMICK. She
  noted Earth Day event could include an opportunity to hold a park clean up or a
  beautification activity. The Concert in the Park in August could also host community
  service organizations to provide an opportunity for them to share their program and
  service opportunities as the concert provides a captive audience and reaches all
  ages. Lastly, she noted that the Parade of Lights could now include an opportunity
  for a Toy Drive in partnership with another local organization. Supervisor Pinuelas
  offered that the Commission could consider potentially moving Movie Nights from
  Thursdays to a Friday or Saturday to attract more people and stated that the
  Concert in the Park would take the place of the August Movie Night.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN asked if the City Celebration event could be used to host
  community organizations as well. Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas
  responded yes and that booths are already offered at the City Celebration event so
  the Concert would provide them an additional opportunity. COMMISSIONER BAIN
  noted that community organizations could also volunteer at the concert, school
  groups and music groups that might be in attendance at the City Celebration event.

  CHAIR POPE wanted to confirm that the concert would take place of a movie night.
  She added that the movie night could add a service component or possible costume
  opportunities.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK noted the Dapplegray area had a Pony Camp
  where people could use the horse ring and had a horse trainer there to educate and
  talk about horses and then allowed kids to participate in a pony ride. This could
  replace a movie night while also highlighting an equestrian activity to the public.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ suggests movie nights be held on Saturdays rather than
  Thursdays. Community Services Coordinator A-Haja noted that the past movie
  nights have been on Thursdays and that they can be moved. ACM Davis noted
  greater attendance on Saturday movie nights in the past. COMMISSIONERS
  MCCORMICK and RETZ agreed.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  7
JANUARY 18, 2022
   COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked what type of event would occur on Earth Day
  and suggested a clean-up that could reach out to trails instead of parks and
  suggested asking Superintendent Goldsmith about any areas needing cleaning
  projects such as litter collection, painting, or light carpentry.

  CHAIR POPE added trash pick-up may not be as available but promotes the Palos
  Verdes Peninsula Land Conservancy’s planting projects which attract the PV Blue
  Butterfly and noted the benefits of seeing the plants grow over time.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ noted combining e-waste clean up with Earth Day. ACM
  Davis noted the Earth Day planning is already in process to have a paper shredding
  event and battery collection at the Peninsula Mall in partnership with Waste
  Management.

  G.  FEBRUARY MEETING DATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas noted the following meeting date of
  February 21st is a holiday and would need to be cancelled. She added that February
  22nd would not be a feasible as an alternated date as the City Council meets that
  night and February 28th would not work as the Equestrian Committee meets that
  night.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI suggested Tuesday, February 15th and the greater
  Commission agreed.

  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas noted the revised date of February 15th.

  7.  STAFF ITEMS

  A.  PERIMETER PATHWAY UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  ACM Davis stated the City Council approved the contract with Wildan Engineering
  and that Wildan Engineering will prepare the plans, specifications, and documents
  for labor and bidding compliance. She added that initial outreach with community
  senior groups was enthusiastic about outdoor fitness equipment and adaptive
  senior equipment. Staff will look at six spaces for senior equipment and report in
  February and order items soon as the project is budgeted for this year.

  B.  PETER WEBER CONTRACT (VERBAL REPORT)

  ACM Davis stated the contract expired in November of 2021 and that
  Staff has worked closely with the contractor on updating the contract. Gill Houle
  assumed the old contract from the City which needed updating with regards to the
  language since the transition. Storm water compliance issues were addressed in
  the updated Agreement. A state-of-the-art barn was built years ago at Peter Weber
  using grant funds which included complying with water compliance. The contract
  should be before City Council for review and approval in February for an effective
  December 1, 2021 date. She stated that they have been a good partner and that
  Peter Weber programs are always included in City program marketing.

  C.  COVID-19 UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  ACM Davis noted an increase in COVID-19 cases due to the Omicron variant. The
  City will continue to work with LA County and Public Health. There are currently no
  restrictions to current programming. Masks are required indoors and outdoors for
  staff. Released today, each household will get four testing kits if they are signing up
  on www.covidtest.gov. There have been no changes with programs and events due
  to being outdoors. The Snow Day was moved to February to avoid high COVID
  numbers as a precaution.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  8
JANUARY 18, 2022
   8.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  A.  ADOPT-A-PARK (VERBAL REPORT)

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK noted the new sign and bench at the Nature
  Center Trail and noted an increase in park goers.
  CHAIR POPE noted that her park looked great.
  B.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)
  COMMISSSIONER MCCORMICK suggested including an event that engages the
  children with horse riding and the equestrian community. Staff can use current
  trainers to promote their sport.
  COMMISSIONER RETZ shared that “Teqball” is a new sport combining soccer
  and ping pong which can be played as single or doubles using a tennis table. It
  may be a sport that could be considered in the future.
